Layer 3 (Network) handles logical addressing using IP and routes packets between different networks via routers.
The PSU converts AC from the wall into the DC voltages (+3.3V, +5V, +12V) required by internal components.
A MitM attack positions the attacker between two parties, allowing them to eavesdrop, intercept, or alter messages in real time.
The CIA Triad — Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability — is the foundational model of information security.
Laptops use SO-DIMM, which is physically smaller than DIMM modules used in desktops.
RAID 1 mirrors data across two drives. It offers redundancy but no performance gain from striping.
A BIOS reset during a power outage can change the boot order. Verifying and correcting the boot order is the quickest first step.
Class C networks default to a /24 subnet mask (255.255.255.0), providing up to 254 usable host addresses.
VGA transmits only analog video. HDMI and DisplayPort carry both audio and video; DVI-D is digital-only.
Thermal paste fills microscopic surface imperfections, eliminating air gaps that act as insulators and dramatically improving heat conduction.
SATA uses a 7-pin data cable for data transfer and a separate 15-pin power cable for power delivery.
DHCP (port 67/68) automatically assigns IP addresses, subnet masks, default gateways, and DNS server addresses to clients.
Device Manager (devmgmt.msc) shows all installed hardware and flags driver errors with a yellow exclamation mark or a red X.
Spear phishing is a targeted phishing attack directed at a specific individual, often using personalized information.
RSA is an asymmetric algorithm using a public/private key pair. AES and 3DES are symmetric; SHA-256 is a hash function.
A firewall is a preventive control because it blocks unauthorized traffic BEFORE it reaches a target system.
Modern CPUs use an 8-pin EPS/ATX12V connector for dedicated CPU power, while the motherboard itself uses the 24-pin ATX connector.
Low or depleted toner in the cartridge is the most common cause of faded output. Shaking the cartridge can temporarily redistribute remaining toner.
LGA sockets have pins on the motherboard socket; the CPU has flat contact pads. Intel desktop CPUs (e.g., LGA1700) use this.
MFA requires at least two of three factor types — something you know, have, or are — making compromise significantly harder.
bootrec.exe with /fixmbr and /fixboot, run from WinRE, repairs the MBR and boot sector.
GPT supports volumes larger than 2 TB and allows up to 128 primary partitions on Windows with UEFI.
NTFS supports large volumes, file-level permissions, EFS encryption, journaling, and compression.
USB 3.2 Gen 2 runs at 10 Gbps. Gen 1 is 5 Gbps, and USB4 can reach 40 Gbps.
An anti-static wrist strap continuously drains static charge from the body to ground, preventing ESD damage.
Dual-channel mode requires RAM in matching (same-colored) slots — typically A1+B1 or A2+B2 per the motherboard manual.
FIDO2 hardware security keys provide phishing-resistant MFA — the physical key is required alongside credentials.
A Trojan masquerades as useful software to trick users into installing it, then performs unauthorized actions.
A pen test simulates real-world attacks to find and validate vulnerabilities for proactive remediation.
TPM is a dedicated security chip storing cryptographic keys and certificates. Windows 11 requires TPM 2.0; it enables BitLocker.
SFC (System File Checker) scans protected files and replaces corrupt or missing files from a cached copy.
Lithium-ion batteries have limited cycle life. If the adapter is confirmed working and the battery won't charge, replace the battery.
VLANs logically segment a switched network into separate broadcast domains without requiring additional physical hardware.
SSH uses port 22 and provides encrypted terminal access, replacing insecure Telnet.
UEFI replaces legacy BIOS and adds GPT support, Secure Boot, large drive support, and a graphical setup interface.
Hyper-V is Windows' built-in hypervisor. Type-1 and Type-2 hypervisors allow multiple virtual machines on one host.
Ghosting is typically caused by a worn fuser assembly that fails to fully discharge the toner drum, leaving residual images.
POST beep codes related to RAM indicate memory errors, often from improperly seated or incompatible RAM modules.
diskmgmt.msc opens Disk Management for creating, deleting, formatting, and managing disk partitions.
Least privilege limits user rights to only what is needed for their role, minimizing damage from errors or attacks.
With a discrete GPU, the monitor must connect to its port, not the motherboard's integrated video output.
Event Viewer (eventvwr.msc) consolidates Application, Security, and System logs for diagnosing crashes and errors.
NVMe M.2 uses PCIe (~3.5 GB/s+); SATA M.2 uses the SATA interface (~550 MB/s). The spec sheet indicates the protocol.
A zero-day is a security flaw unknown to the vendor with no patch, making it especially dangerous.
Cracked glass produces sharp fragments. Safety glasses protect eyes and cut-resistant gloves protect hands.
SQL injection inserts malicious SQL into input fields, manipulating queries to extract data or bypass authentication.

Vishing (voice phishing) uses phone calls. Pretexting creates a fabricated scenario — vishing often uses pretexting.
System Restore reverts system files, drivers, and registry to a restore point while leaving personal files untouched.
Swollen or leaking capacitors indicate failure. They cannot be safely or reliably replaced in the field; the motherboard should be replaced.
BitLocker encrypts entire volumes at the disk level. EFS encrypts individual files. BitLocker protects against physical theft of the drive.
Device Manager reveals whether the trackpad is disabled, missing a driver, or reporting an error. This is the logical next diagnostic step.
NVMe SSDs connect via PCIe lanes — most commonly through an M.2 slot on the motherboard or as a PCIe add-in card (AIC).
NVMe uses PCIe lanes and achieves speeds of 3,500+ MB/s, while SATA III maxes out at ~550 MB/s. Speed is the primary advantage.
Many USB expansion cards require a supplemental power connection (Molex or SATA) to supply sufficient current for connected peripherals.
Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) shows running processes, resource usage, startup items, and lets you end unresponsive tasks.
Windows 10 Home 64-bit officially supports up to 128 GB of RAM. Pro and Enterprise support even more (up to 2 TB on some editions).
100% disk usage is commonly caused by failing HDD sectors, Windows Search indexing, antivirus scans, or background updates hammering the disk.
The front panel header is a small block of pins where power switch, reset, HDD LED, and power LED connectors plug in. It is documented in the motherboard manual.
RIP uses hop count as its sole metric and treats any destination more than 15 hops away as unreachable.
CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED indicates a core Windows process terminated unexpectedly. Common causes are corrupt system files, failing RAM, or a dying boot drive.
An IDS passively monitors and alerts (detect-only). An IPS actively blocks malicious traffic in-line.
NAT translates private (RFC 1918) IP addresses to public IPs, allowing multiple internal hosts to share a single public IP.
Salting appends a random value to each password before hashing, ensuring identical passwords produce different hashes and defeating rainbow tables.
SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) aggregates logs, correlates events, and generates alerts for security incidents.
The incident response process: Preparation → Identification/Detection → Containment → Eradication → Recovery → Lessons Learned.
The CMOS battery (CR2032) keeps the BIOS/UEFI configuration and real-time clock powered when the computer is unplugged. A dead CMOS battery causes lost BIOS settings.
Feature Updates are the major biannual releases that add new functionality. Quality Updates are the monthly cumulative security patches.
Risk transference shifts financial impact to a third party (insurance company) without eliminating the risk.
Task Manager's Startup tab shows all programs configured to start with Windows and allows you to enable or disable them.
ping tests basic IP connectivity using ICMP echo requests. tracert traces the route; nslookup queries DNS; ipconfig shows adapter configuration.
DLP monitors, detects, and blocks unauthorized transmission of sensitive data on endpoints and across the network.
802.11ac introduced MU-MIMO, operates only on 5 GHz, and achieves theoretical speeds up to ~3.5 Gbps.
A honeypot is a decoy system that attracts attackers, observes their techniques, and gathers threat intelligence.
Type 1 (bare metal) hypervisors like Hyper-V, ESXi, and Xen run directly on hardware. Type 2 (hosted) like VMware Workstation run on top of a host OS.
Display Settings allows you to choose between 'Duplicate' (mirror) and 'Extend' (independent desktop across multiple monitors).
DNS cache poisoning injects fraudulent DNS records, redirecting users to attacker-controlled servers.
Mechanical hard drives with spinning platters and moving read/write heads can produce grinding or clicking noises when failing. SSDs are silent.
Restart-Computer is the PowerShell cmdlet for rebooting a local or remote system. shutdown /s is CMD syntax for shutdown (not restart).

XSS injects client-side scripts into web pages served to other users, enabling session hijacking and credential theft.
A CA is the trusted entity that issues, signs, and revokes digital certificates, binding a public key to a verified identity.
POST checks essential hardware — CPU, RAM, GPU, storage — during startup. Beep codes or error messages indicate which component failed POST.
Incorrect keyboard layouts (e.g., AZERTY instead of QWERTY) cause wrong characters. This can be changed in Windows Settings > Time & Language > Language.
A buffer overflow writes beyond a buffer's bounds, overwriting adjacent memory — exploited to execute shellcode or alter program flow.
HTTPS uses port 443. HTTP uses port 80.
An air gap physically isolates a system from all external connections, making remote attacks impossible.
Worms self-replicate across networks without attaching to host files. Viruses require host files; Trojans require user execution; spyware monitors activity.
High idle memory usage is often caused by background services, startup programs, or memory leaks from poorly coded applications.
Disk Management (diskmgmt.msc) handles partition creation, formatting, drive letter assignment, and volume extension/shrinking.
STP prevents switching loops by placing redundant ports in a blocking state while maintaining a loop-free path.
A rootkit operates at the kernel or hypervisor level, hiding files, processes, and network connections for stealthy persistent access.
Proper spacing (air gaps) between components inside the case ensures adequate airflow, which is critical for thermal management and preventing overheating.
System Restore rolls back system files, drivers, and registry to a known-good restore point, often resolving issues caused by updates.
MITRE ATT&CK is a knowledge base of adversary TTPs based on real-world observations, used for threat modeling and detection.
USB-C and USB 3.x ports are the modern standard for connecting external storage devices with high throughput and power delivery.
The chipset (PCH) manages data flow between the CPU, memory, storage, USB, PCIe, and other I/O. It is the motherboard's traffic controller.
Disk cloning software creates an exact replica of the source drive, including the boot sector and hidden partitions, ensuring the new drive is fully bootable.
1000BASE-T requires Cat 5e or better UTP cabling, which supports all four wire pairs at up to 100 m.
Task Manager's Performance tab shows real-time network usage. The Processes tab also shows network usage per application.
A UPS provides battery backup during short power outages, giving the user time to save work and perform a clean shutdown to prevent data loss.
Smishing (SMS phishing) uses text messages to trick victims into clicking malicious links or providing sensitive information.
The BIOS/UEFI boot order must be configured so the USB drive is checked before the internal hard drive. This is done in the Boot menu of the firmware setup.
An A record maps a domain name to a 32-bit IPv4 address. AAAA records map to 128-bit IPv6 addresses.
Each Windows user account has an independent profile containing personal files, desktop settings, and application data, keeping users isolated from each other.
RBAC grants permissions based on predefined roles (e.g., 'HR Manager'). Users are assigned to roles, simplifying permission management.
The Northbridge historically managed high-speed pathways (CPU-RAM-GPU). In modern CPUs, these functions are integrated directly into the processor die.
SHA-256 is a secure hash function from the SHA-2 family producing a 256-bit digest. MD5 and SHA-1 are considered broken for security purposes.
DDoS uses multiple compromised systems (botnets) to flood a target with traffic, exhausting resources and denying service to legitimate users.
A digital signature uses the sender's private key to sign a hash of the message. The recipient verifies with the sender's public key, confirming identity and integrity.
Proper case ventilation with intake fans at the front/bottom and exhaust fans at the top/rear creates airflow that removes hot air and draws in cool air.
ipconfig /release drops the current DHCP-assigned IP. ipconfig /renew sends a new DHCP Discover to obtain a fresh IP address from the server.
Zero trust assumes breach and verifies every access request, regardless of whether the user is inside or outside the network perimeter.
